title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 97
paragraphs: When Xerxes realized the disaster that had befallen him, he feared that one of the Ionians might suggest to the Greeks, or they might themselves conceive the idea, of sailing to the Hellespont and breaking up the bridges; and so he might be cut off in Europe and run the risk of utter destruction. Therefore he began to think about taking flight. But he wished his intention not to be perceived either by the Greeks or by his own side; so he undertook to build a mole across to Salamis, lashing Phoenician merchant ships together to serve him both as a bridge and a wall, and made preparations for fighting as though he intended to have another sea-battle. Seeing this, all the rest assumed he had made himself ready in earnest and meant to stay and fight; but Mardonius did not fail to perceive the true meaning of all this, being very well versed by experience in the king's way of thinking.
